questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.**

It is possible __to prevent oneself__ __with respiratory diseases__ __by maintaining__ __a disciplined lifestyle.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **from respiratory diseases**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace the preposition **'with'** with **'from'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **'From'** is a preposition, that is used as a function word to indicate physical separation or an act or condition of removal, abstention, exclusion, release, subtraction, or differentiation.
 
 
• **Example -** *He is suffering **from** a headache.*
 
 
 
• The main difference between the part **'with'** and part **'from'** is that the phrase part **'with'** is typically used in reference to objects or possessions, whereas the phrase part **'from'** is typically used in reference to people.
 
• Here in the given sentence, **'from'** is used to explain the theme of the passage, that is **"If an individual person maintains a disciplined lifestyle then it is possible to keep him/her from respiratory diseases"**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Hence, the corrected sentence is:** *It is possible to prevent oneself **from respiratory diseases**__ by maintaining a disciplined lifestyle.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The birds flew / fastly above us / as we stood / on our terrace.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is **'****fastly above'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Fastly’** is **not correct.**
 
• The word** ‘fast’ is used in the same form in adjectives and in adverbs.**
 
• Generally, we **add ' ly' to the adjectives to change them into adverbs.**
 
• But there are certain words that can be used **as adjectives as well as adverbs without adding 'ly'.** **Eg:** ‘ fast, straight, enough, etc. ‘
 
• **Examples-** * • He ran fast. (adverb)*

* •They like fast cars and expensive restaurants. (adjective)*

So, the right sentence is**:** *The birds flew fast above us as we stood on our terrace.__*

The correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.**

When you have worked out this sum, you may went out to play.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **went out to play**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **'went out'** with **'go out'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• The given sentence is written in the **Present Perfect tense**.
 
• **Structure of the Present Perfect Tense:** **Subject + have/has + past participle + the rest of the sentence.__**
 
• The **present perfect** in the **'if/when'** -clause of a sentence in the first conditional emphasises that **one action depends on the completion of another**.
 
 
• **Example -** *When I've finished writing my paper by tonight, I'll go out with my friends.*
 
 
 
• The phrase **'go out'** is often used this way to state that someone is going out to do something.
 
• **'Went out'** as a verb means Simple past tense.
 
• The given sentence states that **"After completing the sum, he may go out and play."**

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence: ***When you have worked out this sum, you may** go out** to play.*

• If something is limited it is not very great in amount, range, or degree. 
 
 
• *Example: Book early because there are only a **limited** number of seats available.*

• *Example: Lack of cash is a **limiting** factor.*

 ​

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Sheela __is trying__ for a job since last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **has been trying **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace** 'is trying'** with **'has been trying'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **“Is trying”** refers to occurring in the present, at the present moment.
 
• **Structure of the Present Continuous Tense:** ***Subject + am/is/are + present participle (verb+ing) + the rest of the sentence__***
 __
 
• ​__**Example -** *The boys are playing in the park.*
 
 
 
• **“Has been trying”** refers to the **present perfect continuous**. It refers to a time period which began in the past and continues in the present and into the future.
 
• Structure of the Present Perfect Continuous Tense: *__**Subject + have/has + been + present participle + the rest of the sentence**__*
 
 
• **​Example -** *I have been watching TV since 7 pm.*
 
 
 
• We normally use **'since'** with the present perfect to describe an action or situation that **began in the past and continues in the present**.
 
• In the given sentence** 'since'** is used to mean that **"Sheela is continuously trying for a job for the last year and in present, the search is going on."**
 
• **'Has'** is used with the third person singular.

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Sheela **has been trying** for a job since last year. *
